symbols.name: D
symbols.def: Number of observed system variables.

symbols.name: V
symbols.def: Indices of the observed variables.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: Number of nonobservational regimes.

symbols.name: Kcal
symbols.def: Regime indices, with zero denoting observation.

symbols.name: Kplus
symbols.def: Indices of the explicitly nonobservational soft-intervention regimes.

symbols.name: zeta
symbols.def: Exogenous indicator vertex for nonobservational regime \(k\); no intervention-indicator vertex exists at index zero.

symbols.name: eta
symbols.def: Generic member of Dai et al.'s causally sufficient model family.

symbols.name: Seta
symbols.def: Binary selection nodes in candidate model \(\eta\).

symbols.name: Geta
symbols.def: Candidate causal DAG before intervention and selection conditioning.

symbols.name: Ieta
symbols.def: Candidate target family with the observational target \(I_\eta^{(0)}=\varnothing\) separated from the unknown nonobservational targets.

symbols.name: Tw
symbols.def: Dai et al.'s selected observational graph at index zero and basal-world interventional twin DAGs only at nonzero indices.

symbols.name: Mproj
symbols.sig: \(\operatorname{Mag}(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,0))=\mathcal M_\eta^{(0)}\) on \(V\), and \(\operatorname{Mag}(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,k))=\mathcal M_\eta^{(k)}\) on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) for \(k\in\mathcal K_+\)
symbols.def: Regime-specific MAG projection, with a distinct indicator-free observational branch and indicator-retaining nonobservational branches.

symbols.name: Meq
symbols.def: Two MAGs are related when they have the same adjacencies, unshielded colliders, and collider status on every common discriminating path.

symbols.name: Mfam
symbols.def: Supplied population-oracle MAG representatives: \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) is on \(V\), and \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\) is on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) for \(k\in\mathcal K_+\).

symbols.name: Ccal
symbols.def: All candidate models satisfying the published causally sufficient pre-treatment-selection semantics and whose regime twin MAGs are Markov equivalent to the supplied representatives.

symbols.name: Ecal
symbols.def: Ordered incidence positions \(e=(k,u;uv)\) over the common regime skeletons, one position for each endpoint of each adjacency.

symbols.name: mark
symbols.def: Tail or arrowhead at endpoint position \(e\) in a fully oriented MAG.

symbols.name: PSI
symbols.def: Canonical SI-PAG family whose endpoint marks are the marks invariant over \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\), with a circle at every noninvariant endpoint.

symbols.name: Pinit
symbols.def: The matrix-encoded family obtained by orienting unshielded colliders in every regime and intervention-indicator tails only in regimes indexed by \(\mathcal K_+\); all further within- and cross-regime orientations are delegated to \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\).

symbols.name: Hext
symbols.def: Technique handle combining discriminating-path closure, twin-graph descendant and ancestral-selection labels, and realizability-preserving paired completions.

symbols.name: RSI
symbols.def: Finite rule system to be derived by \(\texttt{oeq:si-extension-calculus}\), containing ordinary within-regime FCI rules and twin-compatible cross-regime rules from handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{ext}}\).

symbols.name: Cl
symbols.def: Least fixed point obtained by repeatedly replacing a circle endpoint by a tail or arrowhead using a rule in \(\mathsf R\), never deleting an adjacency or reversing a fixed mark.

symbols.name: Nend
symbols.def: Maximum number of endpoint positions over one observational graph on \(D\) vertices and \(K\) intervention graphs on \(D+1\) vertices.

symbols.name: Lin
symbols.def: Number of entries in one \(D\)-vertex observational adjacency-mark matrix and \(K\) nonobservational \(D+1\)-vertex adjacency-mark matrices.

symbols.name: arule
symbols.def: Number of regime placeholders in the finite code of rule \(r\).

symbols.name: brule
symbols.def: Number of vertex placeholders in the finite code of rule \(r\).

symbols.name: Trule
symbols.def: Worst-case time for one exhaustive match scan of finitely coded rule \(r\), including cubic-time graph searches for its path premises.

symbols.name: Tclose
symbols.def: Total time to materialize the initial family and run successful rule scans plus the final no-update scan on the encoded oracle MAG family.

symbols.name: CDIScmp
symbols.def: Initialize at \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{init}}(\mathbf M)\), apply \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\) to monotone closure, and return the observational component together with the coupled regime certificate.

assumptions.condition: For candidate \(\eta\), \(\mathcal G_\eta\) is a finite directed acyclic graph on \(V\cup S_\eta\).
Candidate \(\eta\) contains no latent common cause of two vertices in \(V\).

standard.name: Dai et al. binary selection-node convention

assumptions.condition: Every vertex in \(S_\eta\) has no child in \(\mathcal G_\eta\).

standard.name: Dai et al. childless selection nodes

assumptions.condition: Every parent in \(\mathcal G_\eta\) of a vertex in \(S_\eta\) belongs to \(V\).

standard.name: Dai et al. observed-parent selection nodes

assumptions.condition: The observed stratum for candidate \(\eta\) conditions on \(S_\eta=\mathbf 1\).
The conditioned selection-node set in \(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,0)\) and in \(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,k)\) for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\) equals the basal copy \(S_\eta^*\).
The observational regime has empty intervention target \(I_\eta^{(0)}=\varnothing\).
For each \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), every structural mechanism outside \(I_\eta^{(k)}\) and its exogenous input are shared with the basal world.
The indicator-free observational projection \(\mathcal M_\eta^{(0)}\) on \(V\) is Markov equivalent to the supplied observational representative \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\).
For every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), the projected twin MAG \(\mathcal M_\eta^{(k)}\) on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) is Markov equivalent to the supplied nonobservational representative \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\).
The supplied family has at least one compatible model: \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\ne\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Separated observational and interventional twin graphs
definitions.construction: Define \(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,0)\) as the indicator-free selected observational DAG on reality vertices \(X_V\) and basal selection copies \(S_\eta^*\): copy \(\mathcal G_\eta[V]\) onto \(X_V\), copy each selection-parent edge into \(S_\eta^*\), and introduce no basal system copy, shared-noise vertex, or intervention-indicator vertex. Separately, for each \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), form \(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,k)\) on reality vertices \(X_V\), basal copies \(X_i^*\) and shared noises \(\varepsilon_i\) for \(i\in\operatorname{de}_{\mathcal G_\eta}(I_\eta^{(k)})\), basal selection copies \(S_\eta^*\), and \(\zeta_k\). Copy each edge of \(\mathcal G_\eta[V]\) into each available world, route unaffected parents into affected basal children, copy selection-parent edges only into \(S_\eta^*\), add \(\varepsilon_i\to X_i\) and \(\varepsilon_i\to X_i^*\), and add \(\zeta_k\to X_i\) exactly for \(i\in I_\eta^{(k)}\).

definitions.name: Regime MAG projection
definitions.construction: Set \(\mathcal M_\eta^{(0)}=\operatorname{Mag}(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,0);X_V,\varnothing,S_\eta^*)\), retaining exactly \(V\) and no intervention indicator. Separately, for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), set \(\mathcal M_\eta^{(k)}=\operatorname{Mag}(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,k);X_V\cup\{\zeta_k\},X^*\cup\varepsilon,S_\eta^*)\). In either branch, join two retained vertices exactly when an inducing path exists after the stated marginalization and conditioning, then place a tail at an endpoint exactly when that endpoint is an ancestor of the other endpoint or of \(S_\eta^*\), and an arrowhead otherwise.

definitions.name: Regime endpoint domain
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal E(\mathbf M)=\{(k,u;uv):k\in\mathcal K,\ uv\in E(\mathcal M^{(k)}),\ u\in\{u,v\}\}\).

definitions.name: Canonical SI-PAG
definitions.construction: For each \(e\in\mathcal E(\mathbf M)\), set \(\operatorname{mark}_e(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}})=a\in\{\mathrm{tail},\mathrm{arrow}\}\) when \(\operatorname{mark}_e(\mathcal M_\eta^{(k)})=a\) for every \(\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\), and set \(\operatorname{mark}_e(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}})=\circ\) otherwise; retain the common regime skeletons.

definitions.name: Initial regime family
definitions.construction: On the observational skeleton on \(V\), orient the supplied unshielded colliders. On each nonobservational skeleton indexed by \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), orient the supplied unshielded colliders and every endpoint at the existing indicator \(\zeta_k\) as a tail. No indicator endpoint is introduced in regime zero. Store the resulting family as adjacency and endpoint-mark matrices \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{init}}(\mathbf M)\); ordinary FCI closure and cross-regime propagation are both performed by \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\).

definitions.name: Twin-compatible extension handle
definitions.construction: Handle: start from the ordinary discriminating-path and uncovered-path closure inside each regime; attach the descendant and ancestral-selection labels forced by Dai et al.'s twin-MAG lemmas; propagate only label consequences shared across regimes; then adapt Jaber et al.'s I-MAG realizability lemma and Zhang's circle-component completion to construct, for a chosen unresolved endpoint, one tail completion and one arrowhead completion that are projections of a single common basal DAG with one ordered unknown-target family.

definitions.name: Finite oracle-MAG encoding
definitions.construction: Encode \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) by one \(D\times D\) adjacency-mark matrix on \(V\), and encode each \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\), \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), by one \((D+1)\times(D+1)\) adjacency-mark matrix on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\). The representation length is \(L_{\mathrm{in}}=D^2+K(D+1)^2\), and regime zero has no row or column for an indicator.

definitions.name: Finite SI-rule encoding and matcher
definitions.construction: Encode each \(r\in\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\) by a finite tuple of \(a_r\) typed regime placeholders, \(b_r\) typed vertex placeholders, adjacency and endpoint-mark premises, finite-state uncovered-path or discriminating-path predicates, and a nonempty list of circle-to-tail or circle-to-arrow updates. Regime placeholders are typed as either \(\{0\}\) or \(\mathcal K_+\), and an indicator term may occur only with the latter type. Match \(r\) by enumerating its regime and vertex assignments and deciding every path predicate by breadth-first search on its finite product-state graph. One exhaustive scan has cost \(T_r(D,K)=O((K+1)^{a_r}(D+1)^{b_r+3})\).

definitions.name: Monotone rule closure
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathsf R}(\mathcal P)=\bigvee_{t\ge0}\mathsf R^t(\mathcal P)\), where the join is taken in the endpoint information order \(\circ\prec\mathrm{tail}\) and \(\circ\prec\mathrm{arrow}\), and every strict step fixes at least one previously circular endpoint.

definitions.name: Oracle-input closure schedule
definitions.construction: Materialize \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{init}}(\mathbf M)\) from the encoded oracle family by enumerating triples, then scan the finitely encoded rules in a fixed order and apply every consistent match found in a scan. Repeat after each scan that makes at least one strict endpoint update and stop after the first no-update scan. Record the certificate consisting of the ordered strict updates and the terminal no-match result. Its runtime envelope is \(T_{\mathrm{cl}}(D,K)=O((K+1)(D+1)^3+(N_{\mathrm{end}}+1)\sum_{r\in\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}}T_r(D,K))\).

definitions.name: Complete population CDIS
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)=\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{init}}(\mathbf M))\), computed by the certified schedule in \(\texttt{def:closure-runtime-certificate}\), with the observational component on \(V\) reported as the learned causal-selection graph and the nonobservational components on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\), \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), retained as its regime certificate.

statements.statement: For any finite \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\) represented by \(\texttt{def:finite-rule-encoding}\) and monotone in the endpoint information order, the schedule in \(\texttt{def:closure-runtime-certificate}\) terminates after at most \(N_{\mathrm{end}}=D(D-1)+KD(D+1)\) strict endpoint updates and one terminal no-update scan. Rule \(r\) is matched in \(T_r(D,K)=O((K+1)^{a_r}(D+1)^{b_r+3})\) time, and the total oracle-input orientation runtime is \(T_{\mathrm{cl}}(D,K)=O((K+1)(D+1)^3+(N_{\mathrm{end}}+1)\sum_{r\in\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}}T_r(D,K))\), which is polynomial in the finite input dimensions because the rule set and every \(a_r,b_r\) are fixed independently of \(D,K\).
statements.justification: The per-rule matcher and endpoint potential turn finite closure into a checkable total runtime certificate on the supplied oracle graphs.
statements.gap: DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention gives iterative CDIS pseudocode but no finite rule encoding, per-rule matching cost, or oracle-input closure runtime.
statements.consumer: A population implementation can audit every orientation scan and certify polynomial mark propagation without a complexity claim for discovering the oracle MAGs.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{ext}}\), can one construct a finite within- and cross-regime rule system \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\), independent of \(D,K\), such that every rule has the typed finite representation in \(\texttt{def:finite-rule-encoding}\), has per-scan cost \(T_r(D,K)=O((K+1)^{a_r}(D+1)^{b_r+3})\), and is sound over \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\); and such that for every endpoint \(e\) left circular by \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{init}}(\mathbf M))\) there exist \(\eta_e^{\mathrm t},\eta_e^{\mathrm a}\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\) whose indicator-free observational projection and indicator-bearing nonobservational projections agree with every fixed closure mark while realizing respectively a tail and an arrowhead at \(e\)?
statements.justification: The paired global extension is the first proof step not supplied by ordinary FCI, unknown-intervention FCI, or Dai's soundness argument.
statements.gap: Zhang2008CompleteFCI constructs witnesses for one MAG class and JaberKocaogluShanmugamBareinboim2020 realizes one augmented I-MAG; neither preserves a common basal selected DAG and all unknown-target regimes simultaneously.
statements.consumer: Residual circles in the sciPlex2 A549 analysis become certified nonidentifiabilities rather than artifacts of an incomplete orientation list.

statements.statement: The rule system constructed in \(\texttt{oeq:si-extension-calculus}\) is sound and mark-complete on the full class: \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{init}}(\mathbf M))=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathbf M)\). Equivalently, a tail or arrowhead is oriented exactly when that mark occurs in every \(\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\), and every residual circle has the two globally compatible witnesses specified in the open-ended question.
statements.justification: Equality between syntactic closure and semantic endpoint invariance creates the missing canonical representative of Dai's equivalence class.
statements.gap: DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention, Theorem 3 and Section 4, establishes sound CDIS orientations and explicitly leaves completeness and an equivalence-class graph open.
statements.consumer: Any causal conclusion read from an SI-PAG can be audited against the entire pre-selection compatibility class.

statements.statement: For every compatible encoded oracle family \(\mathbf M\), \(\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathbf M)\); the algorithm is population sound and complete, its orientation phase uses at most \(N_{\mathrm{end}}\) strict endpoint updates, and its total oracle-input closure runtime is \(T_{\mathrm{cl}}(D,K)\). The observational output is on \(V\), each nonobservational certificate component is on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) for \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), and no bound is asserted for the conditional-independence or invariance queries needed to obtain \(\mathbf M\).
statements.justification: The result turns the canonical representation theorem into a complete population procedure with an auditable oracle-input orientation cost.
statements.gap: DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention provides only a sound population guarantee for its reported orientations and no total runtime for closing supplied regime MAGs.
statements.consumer: Population benchmarking of CDIS on perturbation regimes gains an exact target graph and a reproducible closure certificate rather than precision against an incompletely characterized output.

statements.statement: For Dai et al.'s two-variable regime family with \(K=1\) and intervention on the first variable, the selected collider model \(1\to S\leftarrow2\) and the unselected directed model \(2\to1\) belong to the same \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\). Consequently, the canonical observational edge has a circle at the endpoint of vertex \(1\) and a tail at the endpoint of vertex \(2\); no sound SI-PAG calculus may orient the first endpoint.
statements.justification: The smallest published equivalence witness fixes a nontrivial boundary that the completeness theorem must preserve.
statements.gap: DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention gives the compatible pair but does not state its endpoint-invariance consequence in a canonical SI-PAG.
statements.consumer: The proposition prevents a complete implementation from falsely resolving selection-induced association as causation in the simplest diagnostic case.

statements.statement: If \(K=0\) and every compatible candidate has \(S_\eta=\varnothing\), then the observational component \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}^{(0)}(\mathbf M)\) equals the ordinary CPDAG of the causally sufficient observational Markov equivalence class, and \(\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}\) reduces to complete PC orientation.
statements.justification: The no-intervention, no-selection collapse is the required standard-case sanity check.
statements.gap: The reduction is classical, but it verifies that the new coupled semantics introduces no extra orientation in the ordinary DAG case.
statements.consumer: Existing CPDAG software supplies a regression test for the zero-regime boundary of the SI-PAG implementation.

sampling_model.design: Population-oracle graphical input; there is no sampling randomness in the proposal kernel.
sampling_model.units: A finite observed vertex set \(V\) shared by one observational and \(K\) soft-intervention regimes.
sampling_model.treatment: The observational regime has no indicator and target \(I_\eta^{(0)}=\varnothing\); only \(k\in\mathcal K_+\) has indicator \(\zeta_k\) and unknown target \(I_\eta^{(k)}\), with intervention after basal selection.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable to the population graphical theorem.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The oracle regime MAG representatives are supplied. Their discovery by conditional-independence and invariance tests is outside the complexity claim.

estimand_functional: \(\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)=\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{init}}(\mathbf M))=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathbf M)\)
target_estimand: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathbf M)=\text{the endpoint-mark invariance representative of }\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3 proves that every directed or undirected mark returned by oracle CDIS is consistent with the true causal-selection model.
The augmented FCI rules recover every invariant endpoint mark in one observational MAG Markov equivalence class.
Theorem 3 proves that \(\Psi\)-FCI recovers every invariant mark for unknown-target soft interventions without selection bias.
The paper gives sound orientation rules and completeness in specified restricted-MAG settings while leaving general background-knowledge completeness open.
Theorem 4 gives completeness for F-FCI under post-treatment selection and latent confounding.

tldr: Selective enrollment precedes intervention in many perturbation studies, so one indicator-free observational MAG on \(V\) and the nonobservational MAGs on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) are coupled projections of one unobserved basal-world DAG rather than independent equivalence classes. The project defines the canonical SI-PAG as endpoint-mark invariance over Dai et al.'s full causally sufficient compatibility class and isolates the open construction of a finite sound within- and cross-regime calculus with globally compatible opposing witnesses for every residual circle. Resolving that extension problem yields mark completeness and complete population CDIS, with a finite matrix input, a cost for matching each rule, and a polynomial total orientation-closure certificate, while making no polynomial claim for conditional-independence discovery.

project_justification.gap: Dai et al. characterize pre-treatment-selection interventional equivalence and prove oracle CDIS soundness, but explicitly leave both a graphical representative of the equivalence class and CDIS completeness open.
project_justification.niche: Ordinary FCI completeness treats one MAG class, and \(\Psi\)-FCI completeness treats unknown soft targets without the basal selection world; neither supplies paired realizations that preserve all of Dai's cross-regime twin constraints.
project_justification.fill: The project isolates a twin-compatible extension lemma, uses it to equate finitely encoded monotone rule closure with semantic endpoint invariance, and packages the result as complete population discovery with an explicit per-rule and total oracle-input orientation cost.

related_work: DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention supplies the published twin-graph semantics coupling an indicator-free observational regime to indicator-bearing nonobservational regimes, the adjacency-and-v-structure equivalence theorem, the two-variable selection-versus-causation witness, and a sound but not complete CDIS procedure. Zhang2008CompleteFCI supplies the discriminating-path and circle-component proof architecture for a single observational MAG class. JaberKocaogluShanmugamBareinboim2020 supplies an augmented intervention-MAG realizability lemma and paired endpoint witnesses for unknown soft targets, but its tail-completeness argument explicitly excludes selection bias. AliRichardsonSpirtes2009 supplies the ordered-collider equivalence criterion that explains why ordinary MAG reasoning must be checked before exploiting Dai's special reduction. VenkateswaranPerkovic2026 and WangDuZhou2025 show that generic background-knowledge closure requires additional dense-graph rules and remains distinct from globally coupled twin realizability. LuoEtAl2026PostTreatmentSelection gives a complete F-PAG for selection after intervention, whose square marks and inducing-node semantics do not represent Dai's basal selection. ColomboMaathuisKalischRichardson2012 is relevant only to a later finite-sample rung; the present kernel begins with finitely encoded oracle regime MAGs and bounds only their orientation closure.
technical_internal_limitation: Independent within-regime MAG completions are not accepted as compatibility witnesses: every completion used by the calculus must be realized by one basal DAG and one ordered unknown-target family. A generic non-two-variable finite obstruction family and its calculus certificate remain open diagnostics rather than theorem contributions in this core.
honest_scope: The theorem-level target is population mark completeness on Dai et al.'s published causally sufficient pre-treatment-selection class, with regime zero projected on \(V\) without an intervention indicator and each regime in \(\mathcal K_+\) projected on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\). The finite rule construction and globally compatible paired-witness lemma are open. The stated polynomial certificate covers matrix initialization and orientation-rule closure from supplied oracle MAGs; finite-sample consistency, latent common causes, post-treatment filtering, effect identification, and the number of conditional-independence or invariance queries used to discover those MAGs are outside the claim. In the no-intervention, no-selection special case, the construction must collapse to the ordinary CPDAG.
